--- layout: page title: "Contributing to ampliseq-lite" parent: "Pipelines" nav_order: 4 permalink: /pipelines/ampliseq-lite/contributing/ last_modified_date: 2024-05-02 tags: [snakemake,16S , how-to] --- # Contributing to ampliseq-lite # Thanks for helping out! `ampliseq-lite` is the Snakemake pipeline the Microbial Ecology group uses to get from demultiplexed 16S/ITS amplicon reads to an ASV table, a taxonomy table and a phylogenetic tree. It started as part of Lena's PhD and is now used by about a dozen people in three departments, so please read this page before opening a pull request -- it saves time for everybody, including you. > **TL;DR** > 1. Open an issue first for anything bigger than a typo. > 2. Work on a branch, never directly on `main`. > 3. Run the test dataset (`make test`) before you ask for a review. Contents: * [Reporting problems](#reporting-problems) * [Setting up a development environment](#setting-up) * [Code style](#code-style) + [Data policy](#data-policy) ← please read this one even if you skip everything else * [Pull requests](#pull-requests) Reporting problems ------------------ Before filing an issue please have a look at the [FAQ](docs/faq.md "Frequently asked questions") and at the closed issues, a surprising number of problems turn out to be caused by an outdated SILVA download. When you do open an issue, include - the exact command you ran, - your `config/config.yaml` (remove any paths that reveal sample or participant IDs!), - the **complete** log of the failing rule, which Snakemake writes to `logs//.log`, and - the output of `snakemake --version` and `mamba list -n ampliseq-lite`. We triage issues on Monday mornings at lab meeting and label them as follows: |label|meaning|who usually picks it up| |---|:---|---| | `bug` | wrong results or a crash | maintainers | |`good first issue`|small and well defined| anyone :) | | `taxonomy-db` | needs a new or updated reference database (SILVA, UNITE, GTDB) | Lena or Sam | | `wontfix` | out of scope, e.g. shotgun metagenomics (use nf-core/mag for that) | – | ## Setting up {#setting-up} You need [mamba](https://mamba.readthedocs.io/ "mamba documentation") (or conda >= 23.10, which uses the libmamba solver by default) and git. On the department cluster both are available after `module load mamba`. 1) Fork and clone the repository: ```bash git clone git@github.com:/ampliseq-lite.git cd ampliseq-lite ``` 2) Create the development environment. It contains snakemake, snakefmt, pytest and pre-commit on top of the runtime dependencies: ```bash mamba env create -f envs/dev.yaml mamba activate ampliseq-dev pre-commit install ``` 3) Run the small test dataset (6 mock-community samples, about two minutes on a laptop): make test If this fails on a fresh clone, that is a bug -- please tell us! ### A minimal config for development Point the pipeline at the test data with a small config file. Keys are case-sensitive and the pipeline does _not_ warn about unknown keys yet (see #57), so a typo in `max_ee` silently gives you the default: ```yaml samples: "tests/data/samples.tsv" primers: forward: GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA # 515F (Parada) reverse: "GGACTACNVGGGTWTCTAAT" # 806R (Apprill) trim: {min_length: 200, max_ee: [2,2], trunc_q: 2} taxonomy: database: silva-138.1 min_confidence: 0.8 threads: 4 ``` The expected-error filter discards a read when $\sum_i 10^{-Q_i/10}$ exceeds `max_ee`, where $Q_i$ is the Phred quality score at position $i$. ## Code style * Snakefiles are formatted with **snakefmt**, Python scripts with **ruff** and R scripts with **styler**. `pre-commit` runs all three, so normally you don't have to think about it. * One rule per output type. Rules that call R or Python should use the `script:` directive and not `shell: "Rscript ..."`, so the `snakemake` object is available inside the script. * Every rule needs `log:`, `conda:` and `benchmark:` directives. A rule without a log file __will__ be rejected in review; we have lost too many days to silent failures on the cluster. * Name rules with verbs: `trim_primers`, `learn_errors`, `assign_taxonomy`. Not `step3b`. A typical rule: ```python rule assign_taxonomy: input: seqs="results/asv/asv_seqs.fasta", db=config["taxonomy"]["database_path"], output: "results/taxonomy/asv_taxonomy.tsv", log: "logs/assign_taxonomy.log", benchmark: "benchmarks/assign_taxonomy.tsv" conda: "../envs/dada2.yaml" threads: 8 script: "../scripts/assign_taxonomy.R" ``` If a run hangs on the cluster, press Ctrl+C **once** and wait; Snakemake removes incomplete output files before it exits. ### Commit messages and the changelog Write a short summary line (max. ~60 characters) in the imperative mood, a blank line, then details if needed. Reference issues with `Fixes #12`. Good summary lines look like Add UNITE 9.0 database download rule Fix sample sheet parsing when sample IDs contain dots User-visible changes also get an entry under *Unreleased* in `CHANGELOG.md`, in this form: ```markdown ### Fixed * `trim_primers` no longer drops reads whose primer starts with a degenerate base (#61). + The taxonomy table now has one column per rank instead of a single `;`-separated string, which makes it much easier to read into phyloseq ``` ## Data policy
**Never commit sequencing reads, sample metadata containing participant information, or anything from the `restricted/` share.** Some projects (the infant gut cohort in particular) include human-associated samples covered by an ethics approval that does not allow sharing outside the university network.
If you accidentally commit something sensitive, __do not__ just delete it in a new commit -- it stays in the history. Tell Lena or Sam right away and we will rewrite the history and rotate whatever needs rotating. Nobody will be angry, it has happened before[^history]. Test data in `tests/data/` are subsampled from public mock communities ([ZymoBIOMICS][zymo]) and are fine to share. Pull requests ------------- Before requesting a review, tick these off in the PR description: - [ ] `make test` passes locally - [ ] new rules have `log:`, `conda:` and `benchmark:` - [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry under *Unreleased* - [x] you have read this document Reviews are usually done within a week. During the field season (May–August) it can take longer because half the group is out sampling lakes; ping us in the `#ampliseq` Slack channel if nothing happens. *** ### Authorship ### People who contribute substantially to the pipeline (new modules, major bug fixes, rewriting the docs) are invited as co-authors on the pipeline paper, with roles described using the [CRediT taxonomy][credit]. Smaller contributions are acknowledged in `AUTHORS.md`. If you think you should be on the list and aren't, just say so -- seriously. [^history]: Twice, actually. Once with a 4 GB FASTQ file, which GitHub refused anyway, and once with a metadata sheet. The second one is the reason this section exists. [zymo]: https://www.zymoresearch.com/collections/zymobiomics-microbial-community-standards [credit]: https://credit.niso.org/ "CRediT – Contributor Roles Taxonomy"

serosurv changelog ================== All notable changes to **serosurv** are documented in this file. We loosely follow [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/ "Keep a Changelog 1.1.0") and [semantic versioning][semver], although _honestly_ the 0.3.0 release broke the API without a major version bump (sorry to everyone whose scripts depended on the old two-vector interface of `seroprev()`; see the migration notes under 0.3.0). Dates are in ISO 8601 format and refer to the day the release was tagged, not the day it reached our r-universe. ## [Unreleased] ## ### Added * `adjust_prevalence()` gains `method = "bayes"`, which fits the hierarchical model of Gelman and Carpenter[^gc2020] so that the uncertainty in test sensitivity and specificity is propagated from the validation studies instead of being treated as known constants. Needs **cmdstanr** (>= 0.7.0), which is now listed under `Suggests`. * New example data `sero_toy`: a simulated serosurvey of 1,200 participants in 8 districts with a known true prevalence, mainly for teaching. + `plot_prevalence()` can facet by any grouping variable via `facet_by =`. ### Changed - The default interval for *unadjusted* prevalence is now Wilson instead of Wald. Wald intervals behave badly near 0 and 1, which is exactly where most serosurveys early in an outbreak live. - Minimum R version is now 4.1, because we use the native pipe `|>` internally. ### Fixed - `rogan_gladen()` no longer silently returns values outside $[0, 1]$; estimates are truncated to the unit interval and a warning is raised (#41, thanks to K. Asante for the report). - Column names containing underscores (age\_group\_5y and friends) were mangled in `plot_prevalence()` legends. ## [0.4.1] - 2024-03-18 ## Bug-fix release. If you used `weights =` together with `by =` in 0.4.0, **please re-run your analyses**: stratum weights were recycled in the wrong order whenever the grouping variable was a factor whose levels were not in alphabetical order. ### Fixed 1) Stratum weights are now matched by name, not by position (#38). 2) `seroprev()` printed "NaN%" for strata without positives; it now prints `0.0%` together with the exact (Clopper–Pearson) upper bound. 3) The vignettes build without internet access (the district shapefile now ships in `inst/extdata`). Effect of the fix on the bundled `sero_toy` data, adjusted prevalence in %: | District | 0.4.0 (wrong) | 0.4.1 |true value| |:--|--:|--:|:-:| | North | 12.4 | 8.1 | 8.0 | | Lakeside | 3.9| 6.6 |6.5| |Old Town | 21.0 | 20.7 | 21.2 | | *all districts* | 11.8 | 11.8 | 11.9 | ## [0.4.0] - 2024-01-29 ### Added * Post-stratification: `seroprev(..., poststrat = census_df)` reweights the sample to known population margins (age group × sex × district). Census margins for the three study countries are included as `census_ke`, `census_ug` and `census_tz`. * Support for **multiple assays** per sample: * `combine_assays(rule = "both")` – positive only if both assays are positive * `combine_assays(rule = "either")` * `combine_assays(rule = "sequential")` – the second assay is only run on samples that were positive on the first, which is the usual confirmatory algorithm in the field labs Sensitivity and specificity of the combined algorithm are derived assuming conditional independence of the assays, which is optimistic. See `vignette("assay-dependence")`. ### Changed * `seroprev()` returns a tibble with class `serosurv_est` instead of a plain list.\ Code that used `res$estimate` keeps working, code that used `res[[1]]` does not. * Arguments renamed for consistency with **epiR**: - `sens` → `se` - `spec` → `sp` - `n_val` → `n_validation` ### Deprecated * `seroprev_old()`, the pre-0.3 interface. It will be removed in 0.5.0 – *really* this time. * * * ## [0.3.0] - 2023-06-02 The version used for the analyses in our 2023 paper in __Epidemiology & Infection__. To reproduce those results exactly, install it with remotes::install_github("ecoepi-lab/serosurv@v0.3.0") ### Changed - **Breaking:** `seroprev()` takes a data frame plus column names instead of two vectors. - The Rogan–Gladen correction is applied by default whenever `se` and `sp` are supplied: $$ \hat{\pi}_{RG} = \frac{\hat{p} + \widehat{Sp} - 1}{\widehat{Se} + \widehat{Sp} - 1} $$ with the delta-method variance of Reiczigel et al. (2010). #### Migrating from 0.2.x 1. Replace `seroprev(x, n)` with `seroprev(df, positive = x, total = n)`. 2. If you grouped results with `split()` + `lapply()`, use `by = ` instead. If you also used test adjustment: 3. Pass `se` and `sp` explicitly; the old global option `serosurv.assay` is ignored. 4. Check that your validation sample sizes are in `n_validation`, otherwise the intervals will be too narrow. ### Removed - The **rjags** backend. JAGS is painful to install on the Windows laptops in the field office and nobody was using it anyway. ___ ## [0.2.0] - 2022-11-14 - First version shared outside the group. - Functions: `seroprev()`, `rogan_gladen()`, `plot_prevalence()`. - Project-level settings can be stored in a `serosurv.yml` next to the `.Rproj` file, e.g. ```yaml assay: {name: "Wantai HEV IgG", se: 0.98, sp: 0.995} ci_method: "wilson" strata: [district,age_group] ``` ## 0.1.0 - 2022-05-03 # Internal release for the Kisumu field team. No changelog was kept for this one, sorry! - - -

Maintainers: Asha Mwangi & Peter Lindgren · release checklist in RELEASING.md

[^gc2020]: Gelman, A. and Carpenter, B. (2020). Bayesian analysis of tests with unknown specificity and sensitivity. *Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C: Applied Statistics* 69(5): 1269–1283. [semver]: https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html [Unreleased]: https://github.com/ecoepi-lab/serosurv/compare/v0.4.1...HEAD [0.4.1]: https://github.com/ecoepi-lab/serosurv/compare/v0.4.0...v0.4.1 [0.4.0]: https://github.com/ecoepi-lab/serosurv/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0 [0.3.0]: https://github.com/ecoepi-lab/serosurv/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0 [0.2.0]: https://github.com/ecoepi-lab/serosurv/releases/tag/v0.2.0

# docker compose stack for the Freshwater Ecology Lab data platform
# Services: PostGIS (field data), RStudio, Jupyter, Shiny (public lake dashboard), MinIO (raw logger files)
#
#   start everything:     docker compose up -d
#   only the database:    docker compose up -d db
#   admin tools too:      docker compose --profile admin up -d
#
# NOTE: passwords come from .env which is NOT committed. Copy .env.example and fill it in.
version: "3.9"

x-logging: &default-logging
  driver: "json-file"
  options: { max-size: "10m", max-file: "5" }

x-common: &common
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *default-logging
    networks: [labnet]
    environment: &common-env
      TZ: "Europe/Stockholm"
      LAB_DATA_ROOT: /data

services:

  db:
    image: postgis/postgis:15-3.4
    <<: *common
    container_name: fieldlab-db
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      POSTGRES_DB: fielddata
      POSTGRES_USER: "${POSTGRES_USER:-lab}"
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro   # creates the schemas + the read-only 'students' role
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER:-lab} -d fielddata"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout:  5s
      retries: 5
    shm_size: '1gb'

  rstudio:
    image: rocker/geospatial:4.3.2
    <<: *common
    environment:
      - PASSWORD=${RSTUDIO_PASSWORD}
      - ROOT=TRUE
      - DISABLE_AUTH=false
      - TZ=Europe/Stockholm
    ports: ["8787:8787"]
    volumes:
      - ./projects:/home/rstudio/projects
      - logger-raw:/data/raw:ro
      - type: bind
        source: ./renv-cache
        target: /renv/cache
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy

  jupyter:
    image: "quay.io/jupyter/scipy-notebook:2024-03-14"
    <<: *common
    user: root
    command: >
      start-notebook.py
        --ServerApp.token=''
        --ServerApp.password='${JUPYTER_PASSWORD_HASH}'
        --ServerApp.root_dir=/home/jovyan/work
    environment:
      NB_UID: 1000
      GRANT_SUDO: "yes"
      CHOWN_HOME: 'yes'
      JUPYTER_ENABLE_LAB: yes     # TODO does this still do anything?
    volumes: [ "./notebooks:/home/jovyan/work", "logger-raw:/data/raw:ro" ]
    ports:
      - 8888:8888

  shiny:
    build:
      context: ./dashboard
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      args:
        R_VERSION: 4.3.2
        RENV_VERSION: "1.0.3"
    <<: *common
    container_name: lake-dashboard
    ports:
      - "3838:3838"
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      DB_HOST: db
      DB_NAME: fielddata
      DB_USER: dashboard_ro
      DB_PASSWORD: ${DASHBOARD_DB_PASSWORD}
      SHINY_LOG_LEVEL: "INFO"
    depends_on: [db]
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits: {cpus: '2.0', memory: 4G}

  minio:
    image: minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-03-15T01-07-19Z
    <<: *common
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: ${MINIO_ROOT_USER}
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - logger-raw:/data
    ports:
      - "9000:9000"
      - "9001:9001"

      # pulls the HOBO / YSI logger exports from the field laptops' sync folder.
      # Runs from cron on the host:  docker compose --profile ingest run --rm ingest
  ingest:
    build: ./ingest
    <<: *common
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint: ["/bin/bash", "-c"]
    command:
      - |
        set -e
        echo "[$(date -Is)] starting ingest"
        python -m ingest.sync --source /sync --bucket logger-raw
        python -m ingest.load --db "postgresql://$${POSTGRES_USER}:$${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/fielddata"
        echo "[$(date -Is)] done"
    volumes:
    - /srv/field-sync:/sync:ro
    environment:
      <<: *common-env
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-lab}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      MINIO_ENDPOINT: http://minio:9000
      LOGGER_TYPES: "hobo_u20,ysi_exo2,  onset_mx2202"
    profiles: ["ingest"]
    depends_on:
      db: {condition: service_healthy}
      minio:
        condition: service_started

  pgadmin:
      image: dpage/pgadmin4:8.4
      <<: *common
      environment:
          PGADMIN_DEFAULT_EMAIL: "admin@fieldlab.example.org"
          PGADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD: ${PGADMIN_PASSWORD}

      ports:

# Runs R CMD check on the phenology package and rebuilds the analysis website.
# Adapted from the r-lib/actions v2 examples + extra steps for the targets pipeline.
# If the windows check fails because of sf/terra binaries, just re-run it. Usually works the 2nd time :(
name: R-CMD-check-and-site

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master, 'release/**' ]
    paths-ignore:
      - '**.md'
      - "docs/**"
      - 'analysis/data-raw/**'
  pull_request:
    branches:    [main]
  schedule:
      # Mondays 06:17 UTC -- catches breakage from new CRAN/Bioc releases before lab meeting
    - cron:  '17 6 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      rebuild_cache:
        description: "Ignore the targets cache and rebuild every target from scratch (takes about 40 minutes, so only do this if something is really broken)"
        required: false
        default: 'false'
        type: choice
        options: ['false', 'true']

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE: yes
  GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_: false
  TARGETS_CACHE_VERSION: "v3"     # bump this to invalidate the cache

jobs:
  R-CMD-check:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.config.os }}
    name: ${{ matrix.config.os }} (R ${{ matrix.config.r }})
    timeout-minutes: 60

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config:
          # fmt: table
          - {os: macos-latest,   r: 'release'}
          - {os: windows-latest, r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,   r: 'devel', http-user-agent: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,   r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,   r: 'oldrel-1'}
          - {os: ubuntu-22.04, r: "4.1.3"}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v2

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          r-version: ${{ matrix.config.r }}
          http-user-agent: ${{ matrix.config.http-user-agent }}
          use-public-rspm: true

      - &sysdeps
        name: Install system deps for sf / terra (linux only)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libgdal-dev libgeos-dev libproj-dev libudunits2-dev

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          extra-packages: any::rcmdcheck, local::.
          needs: check

      - uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
        with:
          upload-snapshots: true
          error-on: '"error"'
          args: 'c("--no-manual", "--as-cran")'

  site:
    needs: R-CMD-check
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      CDS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CDS_API_KEY }}      # ERA5 temperature data from Copernicus
      TAR_PROJECT: main
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with: {fetch-depth: 0}
    - *sysdeps
    - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
      with:
        use-public-rspm: true
    - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2
    - uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
      with:
        version: 1.4.550

    - name: Restore targets cache
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          _targets/objects
          _targets/meta
        key: targets-${{ env.TARGETS_CACHE_VERSION }}-${{ hashFiles('_targets.R', 'R/**/*.R') }}
        restore-keys: |
          targets-${{ env.TARGETS_CACHE_VERSION }}-

    - name: Run targets pipeline
      shell: Rscript {0}
      run: |
        if (identical(Sys.getenv("REBUILD"), "true")) targets::tar_destroy(destroy = "objects", ask = FALSE)
        targets::tar_make(reporter = "timestamp")
        targets::tar_meta(fields = c(name, seconds, warnings)) |>
          dplyr::filter(!is.na(warnings)) |>
          print(n = Inf)
      env:
        REBUILD: ${{ github.event.inputs.rebuild_cache }}

    - name: Render site
      run: quarto render analysis/ --to html

    - name: Deploy to gh-pages
      if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
      uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.5.0
      with:
        branch: gh-pages
        folder: analysis/_site
        clean: true
        commit-message: >-
          Site rebuilt from ${{ github.sha }} by workflow run
          ${{ github.run_id }} (triggered by ${{ github.event_name }})

  coverage:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [R-CMD-check]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with: { use-public-rspm: true }
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          extra-packages: "any::covr, any::xml2"
          needs: coverage
      - name: Test coverage
        run: |
          cov <- covr::package_coverage(quiet = FALSE, clean = FALSE, install_path = file.path(normalizePath(Sys.getenv("RUNNER_TEMP"), winslash = "/"), "package"))
          covr::to_cobertura(cov)
        shell: Rscript {0}
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          fail_ci_if_error: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' && true || false }}
          files: ./cobertura.xml
          plugin: noop
          disable_search: true
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}

# Manifests for the regional respiratory-virus nowcasting service
# Cluster: university research cloud (Rancher), namespace "nowcast"
# Apply with:   kubectl apply -f k8s/nowcast.yaml
#
# Maintainers: Epi Modelling Unit -- R. Haddad / J. Oyelaran
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: nowcast
  labels:
    team: epi-modelling
    cost-centre: "4410"     # must stay a string, the billing exporter chokes on numbers
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nowcast-config
  namespace: nowcast
data:
  # model settings, read by both the API and the nightly refit job
  model.yaml: |
    pathogens: [influenza, rsv, sars-cov-2]
    delay_distribution:
      family: negative_binomial
      max_delay_days: 21
    nowcast:
      method: "epinowcast"
      chains: 4
      iter_sampling: 1000
      adapt_delta: 0.95
    regions: {source: "nuts2", exclude: [FRY1, FRY2, FRY3, FRY4, FRY5]}
  LOG_LEVEL: "info"
  FORECAST_HORIZON_DAYS: "14"
  TZ: Europe/Paris
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
    name: surveillance-credentials
    namespace: nowcast
type: Opaque
stringData:
    SURVEILLANCE_API_USER: "nowcast-bot"
    SURVEILLANCE_API_TOKEN: "REPLACE_ME"    # the real one lives in Vault, see README
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: model-outputs, namespace: nowcast}
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteMany"]
  storageClassName: cephfs
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 50Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nowcast-api
  namespace: nowcast
  labels: &api_labels
    app.kubernetes.io/name: nowcast-api
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: nowcast
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels: *api_labels
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *api_labels
      annotations:
        prometheus.io/scrape: 'true'
        prometheus.io/port: "8000"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: registry.epi.example.org/nowcast/api:2024.11.3
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        command: ["Rscript", "-e", "plumber::pr_run(plumber::pr('api/plumber.R'), host = '0.0.0.0', port = 8000)"]
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8000
          name: http
        envFrom:
          - configMapRef: {name: nowcast-config}
          - secretRef:
              name: surveillance-credentials
        resources:
          requests: {cpu: 500m, memory: 1Gi}
          limits:
            cpu: "2"
            memory: 4Gi
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /health, port: http}
          initialDelaySeconds: 20
          periodSeconds: 10
        volumeMounts:
          - name: outputs
            mountPath: /srv/outputs
            readOnly: true
          - {name: config, mountPath: /etc/nowcast, readOnly: true}
      volumes:
        - name: outputs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: model-outputs
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: nowcast-config
            items:
              - key: model.yaml
                path: model.yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nowcast-api
  namespace: nowcast
spec:
  selector: {app.kubernetes.io/name: nowcast-api}
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: http
      protocol: TCP
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: nowcast
  namespace: nowcast
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "120"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/configuration-snippet: |
      more_set_headers "X-Robots-Tag: noindex";
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
  - hosts: [nowcast.epi.example.org]
    secretName: nowcast-tls
  rules:
  - host: nowcast.epi.example.org
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /api
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: nowcast-api
            port:
              number: 80
---
# Nightly job: pull yesterday's case reports, refit the nowcast model, write outputs to the PVC.
# Takes ~2.5h for the full RSV model with 4 chains, hence the generous deadline.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: nightly-refit
  namespace: nowcast
spec:
  schedule: "30 3 * * *"
  timeZone: 'Europe/Paris'
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 5
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 1
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 14400     # 4h
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: Never
          containers:
            - name: refit
              image: registry.epi.example.org/nowcast/model:2024.11.3
              args:
                - Rscript
                - pipelines/refit.R
                - --date=yesterday
                - "--pathogens=influenza,rsv,sars-cov-2"
              envFrom:
              - configMapRef:
                  name: nowcast-config
              - secretRef: {name: surveillance-credentials}
              resources:
                requests: {cpu: "4", memory: 8Gi}
                limits: {cpu: "4", memory: 12Gi}
              volumeMounts:
                - {name: outputs, mountPath: /srv/outputs}
          volumes:
            - name: outputs
              persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: model-outputs}
...

openapi: "3.0.3"
info:
  title: Regional Food Price Monitor API
  version: '1.2.0'
  # fmt: markdown
  description: |
    Weekly retail prices of staple foods collected by enumerators in **312 markets** across Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Rwanda, maintained by the Development Economics group.  Prices are reported in local currency per standard unit and, where possible, converted to USD at the weekly average exchange rate.

    ## Data use
    * Free for __non-commercial research__; please cite the data paper (see `externalDocs`).
    * Do not redistribute the raw enumerator-level records.
    - Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per API key.

    ## Known issues
    1. Prices for _Rwanda_ before 2016 are monthly, not weekly.
    2. Some markets were renamed after the 2019 boundary revision; join on `marketId`, never on the name.

    | field | unit |
    |---|---|
    | price | local currency per `unit` |
    | price_usd | USD per kg|
  contact:
    name: "Development Economics Group – data team"
    email: foodprices@econ.example.ac.uk
    url: https://foodprices.econ.example.ac.uk
  license:
    name: CC BY-NC 4.0
    url: "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/"
externalDocs:
  description: Data paper (Okello, Brandt & Mwita 2022, Scientific Data)
  url: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-00000-0
servers:
  - url: https://api.foodprices.econ.example.ac.uk/v1
    description: production
  - url: 'http://localhost:8000/v1'
    description: "local dev (uvicorn)"
tags:
  - {name: markets, description: Market locations and metadata}
  - name: prices
    description: Weekly retail price observations
  - name: indices
    description: >
      Derived indices such as the cost of a standard food basket. These are recomputed every Monday,
      so values for the most recent 4 weeks may still change.
security:
  - ApiKeyAuth: []

paths:
  /markets:
    get:
      tags: [markets]
      summary: List markets
      operationId: listMarkets
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Country'
        - name: admin1
          in: query
          description: First-level administrative unit (county / region / province), spelled as in the 2019 GADM release.
          schema: {type: string}
        - $ref: "#/components/parameters/Limit"
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A page of markets
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Market'}
        "401": {$ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"}

  /markets/{marketId}:
    get:
      tags: [markets]
      summary: Get one market
      operationId: getMarket
      parameters:
        - name: marketId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            pattern: '^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}$'
          example: KE-0042
      responses:
        "200":
          description: The market
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Market'
        "404":
          description: no market with that id

  /prices:
    get:
      tags:
        - prices
      summary: Query weekly price observations
      description: |
        Returns one row per market × commodity × week. Missing weeks are **not** imputed; use the `/indices` endpoints if you need a complete series.

        Dates are ISO weeks, given as the Monday of the week.
      operationId: queryPrices
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Country'
        - name: commodity
          in: query
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            enum: [maize_grain, maize_flour, beans_dry, rice_imported, sorghum, cassava_fresh, matooke, milk_fresh, cooking_oil, sugar]
        - name: from
          in: query
          schema: {type: string, format: date}
          example: "2021-01-04"
        - name: to
          in: query
          schema: {type: string, format: date}
        - name: currency
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            enum: ["local", "USD"]
            default: local
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/Limit'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/PriceObservation'
            text/csv:
              schema: {type: string}
        '400':
          description: Bad request, e.g. `from` after `to`, or a date range longer than 10 years
        "401":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/Unauthorized"

components:
  securitySchemes:
    ApiKeyAuth:
      type: apiKey
      in: header
      name: X-API-Key
  parameters:
    Country:
      name: country
      in: query
      description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code
      schema:
        type: string
        enum: [KE, UG, TZ, RW]
    Limit:
      name: limit
      in: query
      schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 5000, default: 500}
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: "Missing or invalid API key"
  schemas:
    Market:
      type: object
      required: [marketId, name, country]
      properties:
        marketId: {type: string, example: KE-0042}
        name: {type: string, example: "Kisumu Kibuye"}
        country: {type: string, example: KE}
        admin1: {type: string, nullable: true}
        lat: {type: number, format: double, example: -0.0917}
        lon: {type: number, format: double, example: 34.768}
        urban: {type: boolean, example: true}
        first_obs: {type: string, format: date, example: 2008-01-07}
    PriceObservation:
      type: object
      properties:
        marketId:
          type: string
        commodity:
          type: string
        week:
          type: string
          format: date
          description: Monday of the ISO week
        price:
          type: number
          description: Price in local currency per `unit`
        unit:
          type: string
          example: kg
        price_usd:
          type: number
          nullable: true
          description: >-
            Price converted to USD per kg using the weekly mean of the central bank's
            reference rate. Null when the exchange rate is not available for that week.
        n_quotes: {type: integer, description: "number of enumerator price quotes averaged", minimum: 1}
        flags:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
            enum:
              - imputed_unit_conversion
              - outlier_checked
              - enumerator_comment

#!/usr/bin/env python3

# fmt: markdown
"""
Wastewater surveillance pipeline -- weekly sitrep
=================================================

Normalises SARS-CoV-2 N1 gene copy concentrations from the treatment plants by the faecal indicator **PMMoV**, smooths each normalised series with LOWESS and compares the trend with reported case counts for every sewershed.  Run it every Tuesday after the lab has uploaded the qPCR results to the shared drive.

Run it as a script

    python ww_pipeline.py --week 2024-W11 --plants ALV BRG

or render it with `quarto render ww_pipeline.py`, which executes the `# %%` cells below and gives you an HTML version with the plots.

What it does:

1. read the qPCR export (one CSV per plant)
2. drop samples that failed QC (inhibition control shifted by more than 2 Cq, or amplification in the extraction blank)
3) normalise, log-transform and smooth
4. write `results/<week>/` plus the Markdown summary that goes into the sitrep

* Author: Ines Carvalho (Environmental Epidemiology), with bits of Malik's thesis code
+ Questions: ask Ines, not Malik -- he has graduated :)
"""

# %%
#| label: setup
#| echo:   false
#| warning: false
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import yaml
from statsmodels.nonparametric.smoothers_lowess import lowess

log = logging.getLogger("ww_pipeline")
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")

DATA_DIR = Path("/mnt/shared/wastewater/qpcr_exports")
RESULTS_DIR = Path("results")

# fmt: off
# Defaults, overridden by --config.  Keep in sync with config/example.yaml !!
DEFAULT_CONFIG = yaml.safe_load("""
qc:
  max_cq_shift: 2.0      # cycles
  min_pmmov:    1.0e+05  # copies/L
  blank_max_copies: 0
smoothing: {frac: 0.3, it: 1}
plants:   [ALV, BRG, CSN, DLF, ESK]
population: {ALV: 412000, BRG: 96500, CSN: 151200, DLF: 38900, ESK: 72300}
""")
# fmt: on

# fmt: markdown
# ## QC thresholds
#
# These come from the national wastewater SOP (v3.2, section 4.4) and were agreed with the lab in January 2024.  If you change them, **tell the lab** and say so in the methods section of the sitrep, otherwise the trend lines shift and nobody notices until the regional team asks why.
#
# * `max_cq_shift` -- samples whose inhibition control (spiked bovine coronavirus) is shifted by more than this many cycles from the plant median are dropped
# * `min_pmmov`: below this the sample is probably mostly stormwater
#   (heavy rain dilutes everything, see the March 2023 floods)
# * `blank_max_copies`: amplification in the extraction blank above this invalidates the *whole batch*, not just one sample


def apply_qc(df: pd.DataFrame, qc: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Drop samples failing QC and return the filtered copy."""
    plant_median = df.groupby("plant")["bcov_cq"].transform("median")
    df = df.assign(
        cq_shift=(df["bcov_cq"] - plant_median).abs(),
        low_pmmov=df["pmmov_copies_l"] < qc["min_pmmov"],
    )
    bad_batches = df.loc[df["blank_copies"] > qc["blank_max_copies"], "batch"].unique()
    keep = (df["cq_shift"] <= qc["max_cq_shift"]) & ~df["low_pmmov"] & ~df["batch"].isin(bad_batches)
    log.info("QC: keeping %d of %d samples, %d batch(es) invalidated", keep.sum(), len(df), len(bad_batches))
    return df.loc[keep].copy()


def normalise(df):
    # N1 copies per PMMoV copy, times 1e6 so the numbers are readable
    df["n1_norm"] = df["n1_copies_l"] / df["pmmov_copies_l"] * 1e6
    df["log_n1_norm"] = np.log10(df["n1_norm"].clip(lower=1e-3))
    return df


def smooth(df, frac=0.3, it=1):
    out = []
    for plant, g in df.sort_values("sample_date").groupby("plant"):
        if len(g) < 3:
            log.warning("%s: only %d valid samples, not smoothing", plant, len(g))
            continue
        x = (g["sample_date"] - g["sample_date"].min()).dt.days.to_numpy()
        fit = lowess(g["log_n1_norm"], x, frac=frac, it=it, return_sorted=False)
        out.append(g.assign(trend=fit))
    return pd.concat(out)


def two_week_change(g):
    """Percent change of the smoothed, back-transformed level over the last 14 days."""
    last = g["sample_date"].max()
    now = g.loc[g["sample_date"] == last, "trend"].iloc[0]
    before = np.interp((last - pd.Timedelta(days=14)).value, g["sample_date"].astype("int64"), g["trend"])
    return 100 * (10 ** (now - before) - 1)


# fmt: markdown
CONFIG_HELP = """
Configuration
-------------

Pass `--config my.yaml` to override any of the defaults. Only the top-level keys you give are replaced; everything else keeps its default value.  A config for the two coastal plants, with the stricter QC we used during the 2023 floods, looks like this:

```yaml
plants: [ALV,  ESK]
qc:
    max_cq_shift: 1.5
    min_pmmov: 5.0e+05
    blank_max_copies: 0
smoothing: {frac: 0.25,it: 2}
```

Keys that are not recognised are ignored __silently__ (sorry).
"""

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
SUMMARY_TEMPLATE = """---
title: "Wastewater surveillance: week {week}"
author:    Environmental Epidemiology Unit
date: "{date}"
format:
    docx:
       reference-doc: templates/sitrep.docx
---

## Summary for week {week}

SARS-CoV-2 RNA in wastewater **{direction}** compared with the previous week at {n_up} of {n_plants} plants. The population-weighted trend changed by {pct_change:+.1f}% over the last 14 days. Plants with fewer than three valid samples in the window are not shown. See the methods annex for details of the normalisation, e.g. why PMMoV is used instead of flow-based normalisation.

Per-plant trends:

{plant_table}

_Prepared automatically by ww_pipeline.py -- please check the figures before circulating!_
"""

# %% [markdown]
# ## Load this week's data and apply QC

# %%
#| label: load
#| tbl-cap: "Valid samples per plant after QC"
def parse_args(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Weekly wastewater sitrep", epilog=CONFIG_HELP,
                                formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("--week", default=pd.Timestamp.today().strftime("%G-W%V"))
    p.add_argument("--plants", nargs="+", default=None)
    p.add_argument("--config", type=Path)
    return p.parse_args(argv)


# inside Quarto/Jupyter the kernel passes its own argv, so ignore it there
args = parse_args([] if "ipykernel" in sys.modules else None)
cfg = DEFAULT_CONFIG | (yaml.safe_load(args.config.read_text()) if args.config else {})
plants = args.plants or cfg["plants"]

raw = pd.concat(
    [pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / f"{p}_qpcr.csv", parse_dates=["sample_date"]).assign(plant=p) for p in plants],
    ignore_index=True,
)
clean = smooth(normalise(apply_qc(raw, cfg["qc"])), **cfg["smoothing"])
clean.groupby("plant").size().rename("n_valid").to_frame()

# %%
#| label: fig-trends
#| fig-cap: "Normalised N1 concentration (log10 copies per 10^6 PMMoV copies) with LOWESS trend, by treatment plant. Grey points are individual samples."
#| fig-height:  6
#| fig-width: 9
#| layout-ncol: 1
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402

fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(plants), 1, sharex=True, figsize=(9, 1.6 * len(plants)))
for ax, (plant, g) in zip(np.atleast_1d(axes), clean.groupby("plant")):
    ax.scatter(g["sample_date"], g["log_n1_norm"], s=8, alpha=0.5, color="grey")
    ax.plot(g["sample_date"], g["trend"], lw=2)
    ax.set_ylabel(plant, rotation=0, ha="right")
fig.tight_layout()

# %%
#| label: write-outputs
#| output: false
#| tags: [outputs,   sitrep]
out_dir = RESULTS_DIR / args.week
out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
clean.to_csv(out_dir / "clean_samples.csv", index=False)

changes = clean.groupby("plant").apply(two_week_change).rename("pct_change_14d")
weights = pd.Series(cfg["population"]).reindex(changes.index)
pooled = float(np.average(changes, weights=weights))

(out_dir / "summary.qmd").write_text(
    SUMMARY_TEMPLATE.format(
        week=args.week,
        date=pd.Timestamp.today().date().isoformat(),
        direction="increased" if pooled > 0 else "decreased",
        n_up=int((changes > 0).sum()),
        n_plants=len(changes),
        pct_change=pooled,
        plant_table=changes.round(1).to_frame().to_markdown(),
    )
)
log.info("wrote %s", out_dir)

---
title:  "Drought shocks and school enrolment in rural Ethiopia"
subtitle: 'Evidence from the Ethiopia Socioeconomic Survey, 2011–2016'
author:
    - name: "Hanna Tesfaye"
      orcid: 0000-0002-1825-0097
      email: hanna.tesfaye@aau.example.edu
      affiliations: [{name: "Department of Economics, Addis Ababa University"}]
      corresponding: true
    - name: Jonas Weber
      affiliations:
        - name: Kiel Institute for the World Economy
          city: Kiel
date: last-modified
date-format: "D MMMM YYYY"
abstract: "We combine three waves of the Ethiopia Socioeconomic Survey (ESS) with gridded rainfall data to estimate how drought shocks affect primary school enrolment. A one standard deviation shortfall in growing-season rainfall reduces enrolment of children aged 7–14 by about 3 percentage points, with larger effects for girls and for households that do not receive transfers from the Productive Safety Net Programme."
keywords: [drought, education,  "human capital", Ethiopia,panel data]
bibliography: references.bib
csl: "chicago-author-date.csl"
link-citations: true
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3
    code-fold: true
    code-tools: true
    embed-resources: true
    theme: [cosmo, custom.scss]
  pdf:
    documentclass: scrartcl
    geometry: ["margin=2.5cm", "a4paper"]
    keep-tex: true
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        \usepackage{booktabs}
        \usepackage{siunitx}
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
crossref:
  fig-prefix: Figure
  tbl-prefix:   Table
  eq-prefix: Equation
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    dev: "ragg_png"
    fig.align: 'center'
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)
library(modelsummary)
library(sf)

panel  <- read_rds(here::here("data", "ess_panel_children.rds"))
kebele <- read_rds(here::here("data", "spi3_kebele.rds"))
n_hh   <- n_distinct(panel$household_id)
```

## Introduction {#sec-intro}

Ethiopia's agricultural economy remains highly exposed to rainfall variability: roughly 85% of households depend on rain-fed crop production, and the 2015/16 El Niño drought was the worst in fifty years [@fews2016; @dercon2004, p. 312]. A large literature documents the consequences of such shocks for consumption and child nutrition [@dercon2005; @hoddinott2006], but the evidence on schooling is mixed. Children may be withdrawn from school to work on the farm or to save on fees, or, conversely, enrolment may *increase* in a bad year because the opportunity cost of children's time falls [@jacoby1997; @shah2017].

This paper uses three waves of the Ethiopia Socioeconomic Survey (ESS) to estimate the effect of growing-season rainfall shocks on primary school enrolment. Our sample contains `r nrow(panel)` child-year observations from `{r} n_hh` households. We find that drought reduces enrolment, and that the effect is concentrated among girls and among households outside the Productive Safety Net Programme (PSNP)[^psnp].

[^psnp]: The PSNP is a public works and cash/food transfer programme introduced in 2005. It currently covers around 8 million people in chronically food-insecure woredas; see @gilligan2009 for an early evaluation of its effects on food security and asset accumulation.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Replication material
All code is in the `analysis/` folder of the replication package. The ESS microdata cannot be redistributed, but can be downloaded free of charge from the [World Bank Microdata Library](https://microdata.worldbank.org/index.php/catalog/lsms "LSMS-ISA catalogue") after registration. Run `targets::tar_make()` to rebuild everything.
:::

## Data {#sec-data}

### Survey data

The ESS is part of the Living Standards Measurement Study -- Integrated Surveys on Agriculture (LSMS-ISA). We use the 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2015/16 waves, which follow the same rural households. The outcome is a dummy for current enrolment of children aged 7--14 at the time of the interview.

### Rainfall

Rainfall comes from CHIRPS v2.0 [@funk2015], a 0.05° gridded product blending satellite estimates with station data. For each kebele we compute the Standardised Precipitation Index for the *kiremt* (main rainy) season, June to September:

$$
\text{SPI}_{kt} = \Phi^{-1}\!\left( G_k(R_{kt}) \right)
$$ {#eq-spi}

where $G_k$ is the gamma distribution fitted to 1981–2010 kiremt rainfall in kebele $k$ and $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF. Following convention, a season with $\text{SPI}_{kt} < -1$ counts as a drought.

![Kiremt SPI by kebele in 2015. Darker colours are drier; dots mark ESS enumeration areas.](figures/spi_map_2015.png){#fig-map fig-alt="Choropleth map of Ethiopia showing the standardised precipitation index for the 2015 kiremt season, with the driest areas in the north-east (Afar and eastern Amhara) and enumeration areas shown as black dots." width="80%"}

@fig-map shows that the 2015 drought was concentrated in the north-east, in Afar, eastern Amhara and parts of Oromia, i.e. in areas where the PSNP was already active.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-balance
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive statistics by drought exposure, pooled sample"
#| tbl-colwidths: [40,20,20,20]
panel |>
  mutate(drought = if_else(spi3 < -1, "Drought", "No drought")) |>
  select(drought, enrolled, age, female, hh_size, head_female, log_cons, psnp) |>
  datasummary_balance(~drought, data = _, dinm = TRUE, fmt = 3)
```

@tbl-balance compares children in kebeles with and without a drought in the survey year. Drought-affected households are poorer and more likely to be PSNP beneficiaries, which is why all specifications include child fixed effects.

## Empirical strategy

We estimate a linear probability model with child and region-by-year fixed effects:

$$
E_{ikt} = \beta\,\text{SPI}_{kt} + \gamma' X_{ikt} + \alpha_i + \delta_{r(k)t} + \varepsilon_{ikt}
$$ {#eq-main}

Standard errors are clustered by kebele, the level at which the shock varies [@abadie2023]. The key terms are defined as follows.

Drought
:   A kiremt season with $\text{SPI}_{kt} < -1$, i.e. roughly the driest 16% of seasons in the reference period.

PSNP household
: A household that reported receiving PSNP transfers (cash or food) in the 12 months before the interview.  Public works participants and direct-support beneficiaries are pooled.

Enrolled
:  The child currently attends primary or lower-secondary school according to the household roster. We do not observe actual attendance, which probably responds more strongly to shocks than enrolment does.

## Results

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Pooled

```{r}
#| label: tbl-main
#| tbl-cap: "Effect of rainfall shocks on enrolment (linear probability model)"
models <- list(
  "(1)" = feols(enrolled ~ spi3 | child_id + region^year, data = panel, cluster = ~kebele_id),
  "(2)" = feols(enrolled ~ spi3 + hh_size + head_female + log_cons | child_id + region^year, data = panel, cluster = ~kebele_id),
  "(3)" = feols(enrolled ~ drought | child_id + region^year, data = panel, cluster = ~kebele_id)
)
modelsummary(models, stars = TRUE, gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared.within"))
```

### By sex and PSNP status

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Effect of a one-SD rainfall shortfall on enrolment by subgroup, with 95% confidence intervals."}
het <- feols(enrolled ~ spi3 | child_id + region^year, data = panel, cluster = ~kebele_id, split = ~interaction(female, psnp))
coefplot(het)
```

### Robustness

1. Dropping the 2015/16 wave, in which attrition was highest.
2. Using the continuous rainfall deviation in mm instead of the SPI.
3. Adding woreda-specific linear trends.
4. Restricting the sample to children who were enrolled in the first wave.

All four leave the main coefficient between [-0.034 and -0.026]{.mark}; see Appendix A.

:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-event
#| fig-cap: "Enrolment around the 2015 drought"
#| fig-subcap:
#|   - "Drought-affected kebeles"
#|   - 'Other kebeles'
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-alt: "Two line charts of enrolment rates by survey wave. Enrolment falls in 2015/16 in drought-affected kebeles but not elsewhere."
for (g in c(TRUE, FALSE)) {
  p <- panel |> filter(drought_2015 == g) |> count(wave, wt = enrolled / n()) |> ggplot(aes(wave, n)) + geom_line() + geom_point()
  print(p)
}
```

The estimates in @tbl-main imply that a one-SD shortfall reduces enrolment by about 3 percentage points, roughly a tenth of the gap between the poorest and richest consumption quintile. @fig-event suggests that this is not driven by pre-existing trends.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Attrition
About 9% of the households interviewed in 2011/12 could not be re-interviewed in 2015/16, and attrition was higher in drought-affected zones. If the households that left were those hit hardest, our estimates are biased towards zero. Bounds following @lee2009 are reported in Appendix B[^bounds].
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}
Girls' enrolment drops by 4.1 percentage points, boys' by 1.9. The difference is significant at the 5% level, consistent with households protecting the education of the child with the higher expected labour market return [cf. @jensen2010].
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
> "When the rains failed, my daughter stayed home to fetch water."
>
> --- Mother of three, South Wollo (qualitative module, 2016)
:::

::::

## Conclusion

Rainfall shocks have measurable consequences for human capital accumulation in rural Ethiopia, and the PSNP appears to shield households from the worst of them. Expanding social protection *before* a drought is declared, rather than after, would likely protect enrolment as well as consumption.

[^bounds]: Lee bounds trim the distribution of the outcome in the group with lower attrition; because our outcome is binary, the bounds are wide but still exclude zero for girls.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## References {.unnumbered}

::: {#refs}
:::

#' ---
#' title:    "Occupancy of medium and large mammals in Kakamega forest fragments"
#' author: "Amani Wekesa"
#' date: '2024-04-09'
#' format:
#'   html:
#'     code-fold: true
#'     toc: true
#' bibliography: refs.bib
#' ---

#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning:   false
library(tidyverse)
library(unmarked)
library(AICcmodavg)
library(here)

set.seed(20240409)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))

dh   <- read_rds(here("data", "derived", "detection_histories_2022.rds"))
covs <- read_csv(here("data", "site_covariates.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# fmt: markdown
#' ## Data
#'
#' We deployed `r nrow(covs)` camera stations (Browning Strike Force, 20 s between triggers) in the main forest block and in three fragments between June and September 2022, at least 1 km apart and as close as possible to the grid points of the 2016 TEAM survey so that the two surveys can be compared later.  Images were tagged in Timelapse by me and two field assistants; every record of a rare species was checked by a second person.
#'
#' * occasion length: 7 days, i.e. 8 occasions over the 56-day deployment
#' * stations that failed before day 28 were dropped (n = 3)
#' + all site covariates are standardised to mean 0 and SD 1 before fitting

#| label: covariates
covs_std <- covs |>
  mutate(
    across(c(dist_edge_m, canopy_pct, elev_m, dist_village_m), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)), .names = "{.col}_z"),
    fragment = factor(fragment, levels = c("Main block", "Kisere", "Malava", "Kaimosi"))
  ) |>
  arrange(station)

stopifnot(identical(covs_std$station, rownames(dh$golden_cat)))

# fmt: markdown
# ### Notes on model selection
#
# I fit the same candidate set for every species, which is not ideal for the rare ones (golden cat: 11 detections in total!) but keeps the chapter readable and was what my committee asked for in the 2023 progress meeting.  Detection is always modelled with effort, because cameras were not all active for the full occasion.
#
# 1. null model, `~1 ~1`
# 2. detection covariate only
# 3) edge, then edge + canopy, then the full model with fragment
#
# Model averaging over the whole set is done with `AICcmodavg::modavgPred()`, see Burnham & Anderson (2002), chapter 4.

species <- c("golden_cat", "blue_duiker", "bushpig", "civet", "genet")

fit_species <- function(sp) {
  umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(
    y = dh[[sp]],
    siteCovs = covs_std |> select(ends_with("_z"), fragment),
    obsCovs = list(effort = dh$effort)
  )
  mods <- list(
    null    = occu(~1 ~1, data = umf),
    det     = occu(~effort ~1, data = umf),
    edge    = occu(~effort ~dist_edge_m_z, data = umf),
    habitat = occu(~effort ~dist_edge_m_z + canopy_pct_z, data = umf),
    full    = occu(~effort ~dist_edge_m_z + canopy_pct_z + dist_village_m_z + fragment, data = umf)
  )
  list(umf = umf, mods = mods, aic = aictab(mods, second.ord = TRUE))
}

fits <- set_names(species) |> map(fit_species, .progress = TRUE)

#| label: tbl-aic
#| tbl-cap: "AICc model selection table for each species. Only models with ΔAICc < 4 are shown."
fits |>
  map(\(f) as_tibble(f$aic)) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "species") |>
  filter(Delta_AICc < 4) |>
  select(species, model = Modnames, K, AICc, delta = Delta_AICc, weight = AICcWt) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

#| label: fig-edge
#| fig-cap: "Predicted occupancy probability against distance to the forest edge (model-averaged, 95% CI). Rug marks show the stations."
#| fig-subcap: ["Golden cat", "Blue duiker"]
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height:   3.5
newdat <- tibble(dist_edge_m = seq(0, 3000, by = 50)) |>
  mutate(
    dist_edge_m_z = (dist_edge_m - mean(covs$dist_edge_m)) / sd(covs$dist_edge_m),
    canopy_pct_z = 0, dist_village_m_z = 0, fragment = factor("Main block", levels = levels(covs_std$fragment))
  )

for (sp in c("golden_cat", "blue_duiker")) {
  pr <- modavgPred(fits[[sp]]$mods, newdata = as.data.frame(newdat), parm.type = "psi")
  p <- newdat |>
    mutate(psi = pr$mod.avg.pred, lo = pr$lower.CL, hi = pr$upper.CL) |>
    ggplot(aes(dist_edge_m, psi)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_rug(data = covs, aes(x = dist_edge_m), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", alpha = 0.5) +
    labs(x = "Distance to forest edge (m)", y = expression(hat(psi))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1))
  print(p)
}

# numbers for the steering committee summary below
gc <- modavgPred(fits$golden_cat$mods, newdata = as.data.frame(newdat[1, ]), parm.type = "psi")
psi_gc <- round(gc$mod.avg.pred, 2)
lo_gc  <- round(gc$lower.CL, 2)
hi_gc  <- round(gc$upper.CL, 2)

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
committee_summary <- r"[
## Camera-trap results 2022 (summary for the steering committee)

Occupancy of the African golden cat at the forest edge was low (ψ = {psi_gc}, 95% CI {lo_gc}–{hi_gc}) and increased with distance into the forest. Blue duikers were detected at almost every station. Detection probability per 7-day occasion was low for all carnivores, i.e. a 56-day deployment is the minimum we would recommend for the 2023 season. Full results are in Table 3.2 of the thesis chapter.

**Recommendation:** keep the 2023 grid, but add ten stations in the Malava fragment where we currently have only four.
]"
cat(glue::glue(committee_summary))

# fmt: markdown
readme_txt <- r"---(
---
title: "Kakamega camera-trap detection histories, 2022"
creator:   [Amani Wekesa, "Kenya Wildlife Service – Western Conservation Area"]
license: CC-BY-4.0
temporal_coverage: {start: 2022-06-01, end: 2022-09-30}
---

# Detection histories, Kakamega 2022

This folder contains the detection histories used in Chapter 3. Each `.csv` file has one row per station and one column per 7-day occasion; `NA` means the camera was not working during that occasion.

Station coordinates are **not** included because of the poaching risk.  Ask KWS for access.
)---"

walk(species, \(sp) write_csv(as_tibble(dh[[sp]], rownames = "station"), here("data", "derived", paste0("dh_", sp, ".csv"))))
writeLines(readme_txt, here("data", "derived", "README.md"))

[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.0000000.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.0000000) [![License: CC BY 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-CC%20BY%204.0-lightgrey.svg)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) [![targets](https://github.com/reef-ecology/caribbean-reef-fish/actions/workflows/targets.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/reef-ecology/caribbean-reef-fish/actions) Caribbean reef fish surveys, 2009–2023 ======================================

Data and code for __"Two decades of change in Caribbean reef fish assemblages after the lionfish invasion"__ (Ramírez, Okafor & Thompson, *in review*). If you are a reviewer: hello! Everything you need to reproduce the figures and tables of the manuscript is in this repository, and the whole pipeline runs in about 25 minutes on a recent laptop (most of that time is spent fitting the hierarchical models in Stan). The repository is organised as a [research compendium](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2017.1375986 "Marwick, Boettiger & Mullen (2018)"), i.e. an R-package-like structure in which the analysis code, the data and the manuscript live together and are versioned together. ## Contents ## ``` . ├── data-raw/ # survey sheets as entered by the dive teams (do not edit!) ├── data/ # cleaned data, created by data-raw/clean_surveys.R ├── R/ # functions used by the targets pipeline ├── analysis/ │ ├── _targets.R │ ├── config.yml │ └── manuscript.qmd └── renv.lock ``` ## Getting started You need R (>= 4.2), a working C++ toolchain for **cmdstanr**, and roughly 4 GB of free disk space. 1) Clone the repository and open `caribbean-reef-fish.Rproj` in RStudio. 2) Restore the package library: ```r install.packages("renv") renv::restore() cmdstanr::install_cmdstan(version = "2.34.1") ``` 3) Run the pipeline: ```r targets::tar_make() ``` Results end up in `analysis/outputs/`, and the manuscript is rendered to `analysis/manuscript.html`. Steps 2 and 3 also work from a terminal: Rscript -e 'renv::restore(prompt = FALSE)' Rscript -e 'targets::tar_make()' If `renv::restore()` fails while compiling **sf** on macOS, install GDAL with Homebrew first (`brew install gdal`) and try again.\ On Windows, use the binary packages from CRAN instead (see [this renv issue][renv-win]). ## Data The main file is `data/fish_counts.csv`, one row per species per transect per survey. Columns: | column | type | description | |--------|:----:|-------------| | `survey_id` | chr | `--`, e.g. `BON-012-20150611` | | `transect` | int | 1–4; each transect is 30 m × 2 m (belt transect, 60 m²)| | `species` | chr | valid name according to WoRMS, see `data/species_list.csv` | | `length_cm` |dbl| total length, visually estimated in 5 cm classes and recorded as the class midpoint | | `count` | int | number of individuals | | `depth_m` | dbl | mean transect depth | Species marked with an asterisk (\*) in `species_list.csv` were only identified to genus before 2014. Biomass is calculated from length with the usual allometric relationship $W = aL^b$, using species-specific $a$ and $b$ from FishBase[^fishbase] (fallback: genus averages). Densities are expressed per 100 m², so for transect $j$ with area $A_j$ $$ D_{sj} = \frac{100}{A_j} \sum_{k} n_{sjk} $$ where $n_{sjk}$ is the count of species $s$ in length class $k$. ### Settings A few choices (which islands, which years, the Stan sampler settings) live in `analysis/config.yml` rather than in the code. The defaults reproduce the paper: ```yaml default: islands: [BON,CUR,ARU] years: {from: 2009, to: 2023} exclude_sites: ["CUR-031"] # destroyed by the 2019 coastal works stan: chains: 4 iter_warmup: 1000 iter_sampling: 1000 adapt_delta: 0.99 quick: stan: {chains: 2, iter_warmup: 300, iter_sampling: 300} ``` Use the `quick` profile for testing (`Sys.setenv(R_CONFIG_ACTIVE = "quick")`); its results are _not_ suitable for inference! ## Survey protocol (short version) ## Every site was surveyed once a year between May and July by two divers: * four 30 m belt transects at 10 m depth, laid parallel to the reef crest * diver 1 counts all non-cryptic fish within 1 m either side of the tape * diver 2 follows ~3 m behind and records lionfish (*Pterois volitans* / *P. miles*) and cryptic species * benthic cover from photo-quadrats every 2 m (analysed separately, see [reef-benthos][benthos]) + water temperature from the dive computer Surveys before 2012 used 25 m transects; these are rescaled in `R/standardise_effort.R`. The 2020 season was cancelled \(COVID-19\) and the 2017 data for Aruba are incomplete because of boat problems. How to cite ----------- > Ramírez, L., Okafor, C. & Thompson, J. (2024). Two decades of change in Caribbean reef fish assemblages after the lionfish invasion. *In review.* > Data and code: GitHub shows a citation under "Cite this repository", generated from [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff).
BibTeX ```bibtex @misc{ramirez2024reef, author = {Ram{\'i}rez, Luc{\'i}a and Okafor, Chidi and Thompson, James}, title = {Two decades of change in {Caribbean} reef fish assemblages}, year = {2024}, doi = {10.5281/zenodo.0000000} } ```
--- ## Licence Code: MIT. Data: [CC BY 4.0][ccby]. The photos in `man/figures/` are © the dive teams and may __not__ be reused without permission. ## Acknowledgements Fieldwork was funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) and STINAPA Bonaire. We thank the many volunteer divers -- particularly the 2015–2018 field crews -- and the CARMABI research station for logistic support. ![CARMABI logo](man/figures/carmabi.png "CARMABI Research Station") [^fishbase]: Froese, R. and Pauly, D. (eds.) FishBase, version 02/2024, www.fishbase.org. Length–weight parameters were downloaded with **rfishbase** on 2024-02-19; a frozen copy is in `data/lw_params.csv` in case the API changes. input.content: --- title: "Questing *Ixodes ricinus* nymphs along an altitudinal gradient in the Šumava mountains" author: - Petra Nováková - "Tomasz W. Zieliński" date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`" output: bookdown::html_document2: toc: yes toc_float: true number_sections: true fig_caption: yes bookdown::word_document2: default bibliography: [ticks.bib, packages.bib] csl: parasites-and-vectors.csl link-citations: yes editor_options: markdown: wrap: sentence canonical: true chunk_output_type: console --- ```{r setup, include=FALSE} knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 300) library(tidyverse) library(glmmTMB) library(DHARMa) library(here) drags <- read_csv(here("data", "drag_sampling_2022_2023.csv")) sites <- read_csv(here("data", "sites.csv")) n_sites <- nrow(sites) ``` # Introduction Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) and Lyme borreliosis are the two most important vector-borne diseases in central Europe, and both are transmitted mainly by nymphs of the castor bean tick, *Ixodes ricinus* (L.). In the Czech Republic the number of notified TBE cases has fluctuated between approx. 400 and 900 per year since the mid-1990s, with a record 847 cases reported in 2020. Over the same period ticks have been found at increasingly high altitudes, e.g. up to 1,300 m a.s.l. in the Krkonoše mountains [@Danielova2006; @Materna2008]. Is this upward shift a consequence of climate warming, of changes in host populations, or simply of more sampling effort at high altitudes? The answer matters for public health, because mountain areas are popular with hikers and vaccination coverage in the Czech population is still only about 30%. Several studies have described altitudinal patterns in tick abundance [@Jouda2004; @Gilbert2010; see also @Medlock2013, pp. 12--15], but most of them sampled only a few sites, and many used a single visit per site and year. Gilbert et al. (2010) concluded that "the upper altitudinal limit of *I. ricinus* is set by the length of the season in which questing is possible." Jouda et al. (2004) found the opposite pattern in one of their three years (cf. Fig. 2 in @Jouda2004), which they attributed to an unusually dry summer. We therefore ask three questions: (i) how does the density of questing nymphs change with altitude; (ii) is this relationship modified by microclimate, i.e. by the saturation deficit at ground level; and (iii) does it differ between years? The two study years were very different. 2022 was among the driest years on record, whereas the spring of 2023 was the wettest since 1961. Prof. Hönig (pers. comm.) called this contrast "almost a natural experiment". We agree, with some caveats (see Discussion). # Methods ## Study area The study was carried out in the Šumava National Park (SW Czech Republic) and its foothills under permit No. 2021/451 of the park administration. We selected `r n_sites` sites along four transects running from the Vltava valley (ca. 450 m a.s.l.) to the main ridge near Mt. Plechý (approx. 1,250 m a.s.l.); site characteristics are listed in Table \@ref(tab:sites). All sites were in mixed or coniferous forest with a herb layer dominated by *Vaccinium myrtillus*, *Oxalis acetosella* or grasses (*Calamagrostis* spp., *Deschampsia flexuosa*). Sites were at least 500 m apart. Mean annual temperature ranges from 7.5 °C at the lowest to 3.9 °C at the highest site. ## Tick sampling Questing ticks were collected by dragging a 1 m² white flannel cloth over the vegetation along 10 transects of 10 m per site (i.e. 100 m² per visit), checking the cloth after every 10 m. Each site was visited once a month from April to October in 2022 and 2023, always between 9:00 and 13:00 and never within 24 h of rain. All ticks were stored in 70% ethanol and identified to species and stage under a stereomicroscope using the key of Estrada-Peña et al. (2017). Larvae were counted but not analysed further. At each visit we measured air temperature and relative humidity 5 cm above the ground with a handheld meter and calculated the saturation deficit (SD) following Randolph & Storey (1999): $$ SD = \left(1 - \frac{RH}{100}\right) \cdot 4.9463 \cdot e^{0.0621\,T} $$ where $RH$ is relative humidity in % and $T$ is temperature in °C. **Field protocol card (laminated version)** 1. Drag 10 × 10 m. Check cloth after each 10 m. 2. Ticks → 70% EtOH, one tube per drag. 3. Record T and RH at 5 cm. Do NOT sample within 24 h of rain! ## Statistical analysis Nymph counts per visit were modelled with negative binomial GLMMs [`glmmTMB`, @Brooks2017] with altitude (scaled), SD, year and the altitude × year interaction as fixed effects, and site and month as random intercepts. Was a zero-inflated model necessary? We compared models with and without a zero-inflation component by AIC; the ZI model was not supported (ΔAIC = 1.8). Residuals were checked with DHARMa [@Hartig2022], which showed no overdispersion (dispersion test, p = 0.41). All analyses were done in R version `r getRversion()`. ```{r model} m_nb <- glmmTMB(nymphs ~ scale(altitude) * factor(year) + sd_hpa + (1 | site) + (1 | month), family = nbinom2, data = drags) m_zi <- update(m_nb, ziformula = ~1) sim <- simulateResiduals(m_nb, n = 1000) ``` # Results In total we collected 6,482 ticks, of which 5,911 (91.2%) were *I. ricinus* nymphs. Adults made up approx. 4% of the catch, and only 9 *Dermacentor reticulatus* were found, all at the two lowest sites. Nymph density declined steeply with altitude in both years (Fig. \@ref(fig:fig-altitude)), from a mean of 42.3 nymphs per 100 m² below 600 m to 3.1 per 100 m² above 1,000 m. The decline was steeper in 2022 than in 2023 (altitude × year interaction: z = 2.87, p = 0.004). Did nymphs simply quest less in the dry year? Partly: saturation deficit had a strong negative effect on counts (Table \@ref(tab:model-table)), but the altitude effect remained after accounting for it. ```{r fig-altitude, fig.cap="Mean density of questing *I. ricinus* nymphs per 100 m² against site altitude in 2022 (open circles) and 2023 (filled circles). Lines show model predictions with 95% confidence bands.", fig.width=7, fig.height=4} drags |> group_by(site, year) |> summarise(altitude = first(altitude), density = mean(nymphs), .groups = "drop") |> ggplot(aes(altitude, density, shape = factor(year))) + geom_point(size = 2) + scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 16), name = NULL) + labs(x = "Altitude (m a.s.l.)", y = expression("Nymphs per 100 m"^2)) ``` Three further results are worth mentioning: - No nymphs were found above 1,150 m a.s.l. in 2022. In 2023 nymphs were found at all but one site, incl. the highest one (1,248 m). - The seasonal peak shifted from May at low sites to July at high sites. This is consistent with Materna et al. (2008) for the Krkonoše mts. - Larvae were extremely aggregated, e.g. 312 of 1,040 larvae came from a single drag in Aug. 2023. | Altitude band | Sites | Nymphs/100 m² (2022) | Nymphs/100 m² (2023) | |:---|---:|---:|---:| | < 600 m | 6 | 45.1 | 39.6 | | 600–900 m |8| 18.7 | 24.0 | | 900–1,100 m | 6 | 2.2 | 7.9 | | > 1,100 m | 4 | 0.0 | 1.4 | ```{r model-table} #| tab.cap: "Fixed effects of the negative binomial GLMM. Estimates are on the log scale." broom.mixed::tidy(m_nb, effects = "fixed") |> knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Fixed effects of the negative binomial GLMM. Estimates are on the log scale.") ``` # Discussion Our results support the view that the altitudinal limit of *I. ricinus* is not fixed but moves from year to year. In the wet year 2023, nymphs were found ca. 100 m higher than in 2022. Is the upward shift reported in the literature then an artefact? Not necessarily: a series of mild, wet years would produce exactly the pattern described by Daniel et al. (2003) and Materna et al. (2008). However, we cannot exclude that host density also changed; roe deer (*Capreolus capreolus*) numbers in the park increased by approx. 20% between 2015 and 2022 according to the park administration (unpubl. data)[^deer]. The so-called "edge effect", i.e. higher tick densities near forest edges, was not examined here! > Very windy, the cloth kept flipping over. Probably underestimates density at site 17. > --- field notebook, 14 June 2022 Two limitations should be kept in mind. First, drag sampling measures questing activity, not absolute abundance, and activity depends on weather (2022 vs. 2023 being an extreme example). Second, with only two years we cannot separate a trend from inter-annual variation. We are continuing the sampling in 2024 and 2025 with the same protocol. __Data availability:__ the data and code are archived at . [^deer]: Counts are based on winter track surveys. They are not corrected for detectability, so the 20% figure should be treated with caution. We thank Ing. J. Novák for providing them. # Acknowledgements {-} We thank the rangers of the Šumava NP for access to the sites, and M. Dvořáková, K. Beneš and L. Wagner for help with the field work in 2022–2023. Funded by the Czech Science Foundation (GAČR, project 22-00000S). # References {-}

I checked that the YAML parses with node's `yaml` and `js-yaml` libraries. That covers the YAML files and the front matter, fenced YAML, `#|` blocks and YAML inside strings in the other files. The Python file parses, and the R file passed a bracket and string balance check only, because R isn't installed here. I didn't run any formatter.

- **No `# fmt: yaml` directive:** that name would make the whole file fail with "unknown embedded formatter". In `python_script.py`, the YAML config string is instead wrapped in `# fmt: off` / `# fmt: on`, and the `# fmt: markdown` strings contain YAML front matter and a `yaml` fence.
- **Directive placement:** each directive sits after a blank line or code. A directive directly under another comment line, like a shebang or `# %% [markdown]`, is treated as plain text.

`github_workflow.yml` has an own-line `# fmt: table` above the matrix include list. The docs say the same-line form `config:  # fmt: table` is allowed, but `/workspace` rejects any trailing `# fmt:` comment in YAML. That could be a real difference from the original, and none of these files test it.
